transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. It's probably just normal stress—I teach high school, so you know how that goes. 

But... well, what finally made me come in is this physical tightness. My neck, my shoulders, and even my jaw are just tight almost all the time now. It feels a bit silly to complain about, honestly, but it's like I'm constantly bracing for bad news. And it happens even when I'm just sitting at my desk grading papers, or trying to watch TV at night. I just can't seem to loosen up. 

Does that... does that make sense as a reason to come in? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you feel anxious when you experience this physical tightness?

Yes, I suppose so. Um, I don't want to sound like I'm making a mountain out of a molehill, because I know everyone has responsibilities. But my mind just... it never really stops jumping around. 

I'll be sitting there feeling all tense, and I'm stressing over whether the contractors we hired missed something in the house. And then right away, it shifts to work—worrying if my lesson plans are slipping, or if the kids in the robotics club are falling behind. And... well, I guess the hardest part to admit is that I just worry I'm disappointing my wife and my family by not keeping everything perfectly under control. I really try to be the one who holds it all together, so it's embarrassing to feel this worked up over everyday things. 

Does that... is that the kind of anxious you mean? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you find that you worry about these things all the time, or only in specific situations?

Well, it's... it's pretty much all the time lately. I mean, I know I shouldn't let it get to me, but it's been like this for, oh, maybe about seven months now? 

It really started when a pipe burst at the house. We had to do all this remodeling, and it just threw everything into complete chaos. I tried to just roll with it, you know, be the steady one, but ever since then, the worry just kind of stuck around. Even when things are quiet, my brain is just... humming. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm just complaining about home repairs. I know lots of people deal with worse. Is that... does that timeline help at all with what you're looking for?
Do you worry about a wide range of things, or is it mostly focused on a few specific areas like work or home?

Well, it's... I guess it kind of spreads to a wide range of things, if I'm being completely honest. I really try not to let it, I promise. 

Like, I can tell myself to just stop and focus on the class right in front of me—just do my job, you know? But then... one small thought will pop into my head. It could be about a late invoice for the house repairs, or just a student falling behind in my class. And it just sets off this whole chain of what-ifs. I try so hard to push it away, but I just can't seem to shut it down once it starts. 

It's a bit embarrassing, really, being a grown man and getting so carried away by such minor things. I really should be better at managing it, and I'm sorry if I'm making it sound worse than it is. Does that... am I answering your question right? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you find yourself repeatedly thinking about the same thoughts or mental images, even when you try to distract yourself or stop thinking about them?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I hope I'm understanding you right, but it's not really like a single image or the exact same thought playing on a loop. 

It's more... well, like I was saying before, it just kind of jumps from one thing to the next. The what-ifs. But not a repetitive picture in my mind, no. I haven't really noticed anything like that. 

Is that... does that help at all? I'm sorry if I'm not describing things very well, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Have you found that your worrying or physical tension has been interfering with your daily life, such as your relationships or your ability to work?

Well, I... I really hate to admit this, to be honest. I've always prided myself on being reliable, especially for my students. But, um... I suppose it has been affecting things a little bit. 

I've actually started falling behind on my lesson prep and... and the grading is piling up a bit more than usual. I mean, I'm still getting the important things done, I promise! Just... maybe not as well or as quickly as I should be. 

And outside of school, I usually help manage things for the local community theater, but I actually had to step back and give up parts of that recently. I just couldn't keep up with all of it anymore with my mind constantly racing. I feel terrible letting people down like that. I know I just need to try harder to push through it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely incapable or like I'm just making excuses for being disorganized. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
How much distress do you feel your worrying and physical tension are causing you?

Well, I mean... it's distressing, sure, but I don't want to make it sound like it's ruining my life or anything. I'm getting by. 

It's just... it is tiring. The constant tension in my shoulders and the feeling like I'm always on edge. It does wear me down a bit by the end of the day. But I know other people have it so much worse, and I really shouldn't complain. I'm just a bit overwhelmed, that's all. 

I try to just keep a smile on and push through, you know? I don't want to be a burden or make a big fuss out of nothing. Am I... is that the kind of thing you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture without sounding like a complainer.
Have you noticed any difficulties in your relationships with your wife, family, or friends due to your worrying or physical tension?

Well, I... I don't think so. I mean, my wife is wonderful, and she's very patient with me. We get along fine, really. 

I suppose I might be a little quieter than usual when I'm feeling really tense, or maybe I don't go out with friends quite as much as I used to. But it hasn't caused any real problems or arguments, I promise. I try very hard not to let my stress spill over onto anyone else. It's my issue, and I wouldn't want to drag them down with it. 

So, no, I wouldn't say there are any major difficulties. We're all doing okay. Does that... I hope that answers what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you had to take any days off from work due to your worrying or physical tension?

Oh, no, no. I haven't taken any days off. I... I really try to be there for my students every single day. They need that consistency, you know? 

Even if I'm feeling a bit... wound up, or my shoulders are really aching from all the tension, I always make sure to show up. I'd feel just awful calling in sick if I wasn't, well, actually laid up in bed with a fever or something like that. I just put on a brave face and push through it. I wouldn't want to leave the school short-staffed or make extra work for the other teachers who'd have to cover my classes. That wouldn't be fair to them.

I hope that's the right way to handle it? I just try to be responsible and not let this affect my attendance. Is that... does that answer your question alright?
Have you experienced any other physical symptoms besides the tightness in your neck, shoulders, and jaw?

Well... I suppose there is one other thing, though I really don't want to sound lazy or anything. I know teaching takes it out of you. But... I do get quite tired. By the time the last bell rings, I just feel completely wrung out. And it's... well, it's in a way that a decent night's sleep or just having a quiet Sunday doesn't really seem to fix. 

Even just sitting down to grade a short stack of quizzes, it feels like I'm pushing through mud. I always get them done, of course! I'd never let my students down, and I make sure they get their grades back on time. It just takes a bit more effort lately, that's all. 

I hope I'm not just complaining about normal aging or a typical work week... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right details.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your overall performance or effectiveness as a teacher since your symptoms started?

Well... I mean, I try very, very hard to keep everything running smoothly. I really do. The students are my top priority. But... I suppose if I'm being completely honest... I might be just a little bit behind on things. 

It's nothing terrible, I promise! Just... well, my lesson prep takes me a lot longer now, and I've gotten a bit backed up on grading some of the longer assignments. I always get them done eventually, though! I just... I feel terrible about it, because I know the kids are waiting on that feedback. 

And, um, I actually had to step back a little from the community theater group I usually help manage. I just... I couldn't seem to juggle it all anymore without feeling like I was dropping the ball everywhere. I really hated letting them down, but I had to make sure my classes came first. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible teacher. I'm really trying my best to stay on top of it all. Does that... is that the kind of change you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly.
Have you noticed any significant difficulty in completing tasks or making decisions due to your worrying or tension?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I have difficulty completing tasks. I mean, like I said, I might be a little slower with the grading right now, but I always get it done. I'm very careful about that. 

As for making decisions... well, I suppose I do think things through quite a bit. Maybe a bit more than I used to. I just want to be absolutely sure I'm making the right choice, especially when it comes to the students. I wouldn't want to make a mistake that could affect them. So, I might weigh the options a little longer, just to be safe. 

But I wouldn't call it a difficulty, exactly. Just... being thorough, I hope? I try very hard to be thorough. Is that... does that sound alright? I hope I'm not giving you the wrong idea.
Have you felt like your worrying or tension has significantly impacted your ability to enjoy or perform daily activities?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's impacted my ability to *enjoy* things, exactly. I mean, I still love teaching, and I still look forward to seeing my students every day. I really do. 

And as for performing daily activities... I still get up, get dressed, go to work, cook dinner... all the normal things. I suppose I might not be, you know, whistling while I work as much as I used to, but I'm still doing everything I'm supposed to do. 

I just... I might be a little more tired at the end of the day, like I mentioned before. But I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing or letting my life fall apart! I'm definitely still functioning just fine. I hope that's... I hope that answers your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.
Have you been avoiding any activities or situations because of your worrying or tension?

Oh, goodness, no. I really try my best not to do that. I know it's so important to keep showing up, especially for the students and my colleagues. I wouldn't ever want to leave anyone in a lurch just because I was feeling a little tense. 

I mean, I know I mentioned stepping back from the community theater earlier, but that was really just to make sure I had enough time for my lesson plans and grading, not because I was hiding from it! I still go to all the faculty meetings, parent-teacher conferences, the grocery store... all of that. I face things head-on, even if I'm a bit worried about how they'll go. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just really pride myself on being reliable for the people who count on me. Am I explaining that clearly enough for you?
How long have you been experiencing the physical tightness in your neck, shoulders, and jaw?

Oh, um... let me think. I suppose it's been going on for... well, about seven months now? Yes, right around seven months. We had a bit of an incident at home—a pipe burst, unfortunately. And the remodeling after that just... well, it threw the house into chaos. 

I think that's when I first started noticing the tightness. It's just normal stress from living in a construction zone, really, nothing too terrible. I try not to make a fuss about it, since these things happen to everyone, you know? 

Does that timeline make sense to you for this sort of thing? I hope I'm giving you the right details, I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Have you experienced any other physical symptoms besides the tightness in your neck, shoulders, and jaw, such as headaches or stomach problems?

Oh, no, nothing like that. I've been very lucky in that regard. My stomach has always been pretty strong, thankfully. And I really don't get headaches... maybe a very mild one every once in a great while, but just the normal kind you'd get if you skipped a cup of coffee or stared at a computer screen too long. 

So, no, it's really just the tightness in my shoulders and jaw that I mentioned. The rest of me is holding up just fine! I try to take good care of myself, you know, eating right and all that. I hope that's what you were looking for? I'm trying to be as thorough as I can for you.
Do you often have trouble relaxing and calming your mind when you're not actively dealing with a stressful situation?

Well, I... I do try my best to just unwind when I have a quiet moment. I certainly don't want you to think I'm just sitting around fretting all day! But, um... I suppose it can be a little tricky to completely clear my head sometimes. 

Like, I can tell myself to just stop and focus on the class right in front of me, you know? But then... one small thought will just pop in. Maybe it's a late invoice from the remodel, or just a thought about a student who's falling a bit behind. And before I know it, it just sets off this whole chain of 'what-ifs' that I just... I can't seem to shut down, no matter how hard I try to be reasonable about it. 

I really try to keep it under control and stay positive, though. Is that... is that the sort of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just want to be honest with you.
Do you think your worrying about your physical symptoms, like the tightness in your neck and shoulders, is disproportionate to the actual impact those symptoms have on your daily life?

Oh, um... well, no, I don't think so. I really don't spend much time worrying about the tightness itself, to be honest. It's just sort of... there, you know? Like a stiff neck from sleeping funny. 

I certainly don't let it stop me from doing what I need to do. I still go to work, I still teach my classes, I still get things done around the house. It's just a minor annoyance, really. I try not to complain about it or make a big deal out of it. 

I mean, I'm sure people deal with much worse every day, right? So I just try to power through and not let it bother me too much. Does that sound... normal to you? I hope I'm not coming across as someone who just complains about every little ache and pain.
Do you think about your physical symptoms, like the tightness in your neck and shoulders, more than would be expected, given how much they actually affect your daily life?

I... well, I think I just answered that, didn't I? Um, maybe I didn't explain it very well. Let me try again. 

No, I really don't dwell on the physical stuff. The tightness is just... it's just a thing that happens, you know? Like I said, I don't let it get in the way of my teaching or my life. I'm not the kind of person who sits around obsessing over every little twinge. I try to be very practical about it. 

I hope I'm understanding your question correctly this time? I really don't want to waste your time by repeating myself, I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I making sense?
Do you often find yourself worrying that your physical symptoms, like the tightness in your neck and shoulders, might be a sign of a more serious underlying illness?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I really don't jump to conclusions like that. I know some people might immediately think the worst, but I... I try to be very level-headed about it. 

I mean, I know I'm 55, and you get aches and pains at this age, right? It's just stress from grading papers or, you know, carrying heavy bags of supplies for the classroom. I certainly don't sit around convincing myself I have some terrible disease. I wouldn't want you to think I'm a hypochondriac or anything like that! 

I just assume it's normal wear and tear. That's the right way to look at it, isn't it? I just try to keep a positive attitude and not let my imagination run away with me.
